title: Fastpath staging for KV cache: asymmetric FP8/INT8 quantization experiments and calibration loop
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Run and validate a staged quantization strategy for KV cache where short-context requests use an INT8 "fastpath" and longer contexts fall back to FP8. Goal: measure latency wins and quality regressions, refine calibration workflow that includes synthetic drift injection and holdout prompt evaluation.
background: We have several KV quantization experiments (INT8 vs FP8) but customers with latency-sensitive short-sequence workloads report higher P90/P99 variance. Hypothesis: a dedicated fastpath optimized for INT8 on short sequences can reduce median and lower-tail latency while keeping quality regressions within tolerable limits. This ticket explores asymmetric staging (INT8 for recent KV blocks, FP8 for older blocks), end-to-end calibration, and validation against our eval suite.
experiment_hypothesis: A per-block asymmetric quantization policy plus a short-sequence INT8 fastpath will reduce median token latency by >=18% and cost by ~12% with <=0.8% quality regression on the holdout prompt suite after bias-corrected calibration.
calibration_workflow: 1) Offline calibration: collect activation histograms per-layer and per-block across training-like traces; 2) Fit per-block scale/zero-point with asymmetric min-max + MSE bias correction; 3) Synthetic drift injection: perturb activation distributions with scaled noise and token-drop patterns to simulate production drift; 4) Holdout evaluation: run full generation on 12 curated prompts (conversational, code, summarization) and compute token-level perplexity and semantic similarity; 5) Online probe: lightweight sampler that collects 1% requests to run full FP8 baseline for drift detection and retrain scales.
test_plan: - Baseline: FP8 everywhere (current candidate) and full FP16 baseline for quality reference. - Variants: (A) INT8 fastpath for last N KV blocks (N=1,2,4), (B) INT8 without bias-correction, (C) INT8 with per-block bias-correction, (D) staged FP8->INT8 switchover threshold based on sequence length. - Run throughput and tail-latency benchmarks on p4d and A100 pools with realistic request mix. - Run holdout prompt suite and compute delta-perplexity, ROUGE/BLEU where applicable, and embedding-sim similarity. - Run 48h drift simulation with injected distribution shifts and measure calibration stability.
metrics: - Latency: p50/p90/p95/p99 generation token latency and per-request end-to-end latency. - Cost: tokens/sec per GPU and estimated $/1M tokens. - Quality: delta perplexity vs FP16, semantic similarity (embedding cosine), task-specific metrics (ROUGE for summarization, exact match for code generation samples). - Stability: frequency of retrain triggers from online probe and calibration drift over time.
progress_updates: 2026-03-02: Initial experiment harness implemented (per-block quantize/dequantize hooks + perf counters). Baseline FP8 runs collected for 10k requests on p4d-staging.
2026-03-05: Implemented INT8 fastpath for last-2 KV blocks. Observed median token latency reduce ~20% but p99 increased ~7%—investigating dequantization cost and lock contention in fused kernels.
2026-03-07: Calibration pipeline added: per-block min-max + MSE bias-correction step. Re-ran holdout suite; preliminary quality regressions dropped from 1.6% to 0.7% delta-perplexity.

2026-03-10: Synthetic drift harness completed. Drift scenarios (scale shifts and token deletion) show INT8 without bias-correction degrades faster; bias-corrected INT8 holds within SLA for 36h in two scenarios.

2026-03-12: Kernel-level profiling shows dequantization path for fused-attention steals ~3ms per token at high concurrency. Spike source: thread-level mutex around per-block cache refill. Proposed fix: kernel fusion and lock-free ring buffer for KV insertion.
2026-03-12: PR created for bias-correction utilities and drift tester: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/3124
blockers: Perf regression at p99 due to dequantization overhead—needs kernel engineering support (ENG-43321 assigned).
Need updated microkernel that supports combined dequantize+attention matmul for INT8 fastpath (dependency: ENG-41675).
decisions: Use asymmetric staging (INT8 for last N=1..4 blocks) rather than uniform INT8 across entire KV to limit quantization noise for long contexts.
Adopt per-block MSE bias-correction as default in calibration pipeline (applied offline and periodically refreshed online).
Keep online probe sampling at 1% of traffic for drift detection during initial rollout to control cost.
next_steps: ENG-kernel team to prototype fused dequantize+attention kernel (ENG-43321) — target: reduce dequantize overhead by >=60%.
Add per-workload holdout sets and extend evaluation to the internal regression dashboard for automated daily runs.
Run staged canary: route 5% of p4d production traffic through INT8 fastpath with bias-correction and online probe enabled; monitor latency and SLOs for 72h.
Finalize acceptance criteria and schedule a review with PM and Security for release tagging in runtime-2.3.
acceptance_criteria: Median token latency improvement >= 15% vs FP8 baseline on short-sequence workload mix.
Delta perplexity <= 0.8% vs FP16 baseline on holdout prompt suite after calibration.
P99 token latency not degraded more than 5% vs FP8 baseline after kernel fixes and staging.
Calibration retrain trigger rate <= 1 per 7 days under simulated drift scenarios.
Documentation: calibration playbook + runbook for canary rollback published to Confluence.
notes: Compare this strategy against existing tiered-precision proposals (see ENG-25789 and ENG-33145) — this ticket focuses on operational fastpath and online drift detection rather than exhaustive per-layer profiling.
If fused kernel work is delayed, fall back to a conservative N=1 fastpath to bound p99 impact, and increase caching of dequantized blocks for reuse.
